Subject: Data retention exception request - Acme Health

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- Use case: clinical-document summarization for internal care teams; PHI touches name + identifiers in free text.
- Volume: ~120k messages/mo, mixed short and long docs; real-time latency target < 750ms p50.
- Primary asks from security/compliance: zero retention for PII logs (no request/response storage), shortened operational logs (7-day TTL), and EU data residency for backups (if any).

We discussed options: Redwood Private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed KMS, and an exception path for custom retention schedules if Private isn't an option immediately. Attached is the data-retention-exception-form for your team to fill (fields we need: types of PII, expected TTLs, legal owner, and audit contacts). Also attached our SOC 2 summary and sample audit logs format.

Next steps I propose:
1) You and security review the attached form and indicate the required retention windows (due 2027-04-15).
2) Marissa to scope technical approach and confirm if we can provide a 0-retention pipeline for request/response bodies while keeping short-term operational traces.
3) Rafael to map the changes required for our logging pipeline and produce a one-page impact/risks doc.

If it helps, we can schedule a 30-min security deep-dive later this week.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes

Camila —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the ask with Security: 

- Priority: zero retention for any request/response payloads that contain PHI. We cannot have those stored in any logs or object stores.
- Operational traces (request IDs, basic response times, error codes) can be retained for 7 days, but no stack traces or payloads containing PHI.
- We need an explicit guarantee about backup behavior (no backups of request/response bodies). Any metadata backups should be EU-resident for at-rest copies.

Questions: 
1) Is 0-retention for request/response bodies achievable on Hosted API or do we need Private?
2) What changes would impact observability and incident response if we remove request/response retention?

We're aiming to close the procurement conversation quickly but need the above confirmed before legal signs anything. We'll review the attached form and get it back by Friday.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Data Security | Acme Health
daniel.park@acmehealth.com

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the clear requirements — we can support this, but there are trade-offs to be explicit about so Legal and Security can evaluate risk quickly. High-level: 

- Hosted API: we can offer "ephemeral mode" where request/response payloads containing PII are not written to long-term storage. In practice this means:
  - Request/response bodies are processed in-memory and not persisted.
  - Short-lived traces (request IDs, timing, status codes) are emitted to ops logs with a 7-day TTL.
  - We will ensure backups do not contain request/response bodies; snapshots of metrics/aggregates may still be stored (no PHI).

- Private (VPC/on-prem): provides stronger guarantees because the customer can control storage and backups; 0-retention policy can be enforced at the customer side with our guidance.

Operational impact:
- Incident response: without full request/response bodies, reproducing issues that depend on payload content is harder. We recommend a canary capture workflow where, for high-priority incidents, we can temporarily enable capture under strict access controls and immediate deletion after triage (documented mutual action plan).
- Auditing: we'll provide structured audit logs (who/when/what) that do not contain PII, and an attestations pack for your SOC2/ISO review.

Next steps from our side (I can take items 2 & 3):
- Rafael will produce a 1-page impact/risk doc and a proposed canary incident workflow (delivery 2027-04-13).
- I'll draft contract language for an Appendix to the SOW that enshrines the 0-retention exception and the canary process.
- Camila, can you send the HubSpot deal link and the DocuSign template so Legal can route?

Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Data retention exception request - Acme Health

Daniel / team —

I put together the 1-pager and the canary workflow as promised. Summary:

- Feasibility: We can implement 0-retention for request/response bodies on the Hosted API by routing PHI-marked requests through an in-memory-only processing path; nothing is written to object storage and traces containing payloads are suppressed. This requires a small middleware change and tagging at the client side to mark PHI payloads (we can do server-side classification if you prefer, but that expands attack surface).

- Canary workflow for incident triage:
  1) Incident declared by Acme/Redwood on agreed channel.
  2) Temporary capture enabled for a narrowly-scoped request set (timeboxed, access-controlled, encrypted at rest).
  3) Joint triage within 24 hours.
  4) Immediate deletion of captured bodies with signed confirmation.

- Risk/impacts:
  - Reduced debugging fidelity for rare edge cases.
  - Increased time-to-resolution on complex model-failure incidents.
  - No impact to billing, throughput, or SLA if agreed workflows are followed.

I've attached the one-pager as a PDF and included the config snippet we would add to the client SDK (we will share a PR-ready branch once you approve).

Next actions for Acme:
- Please confirm you accept the canary workflow and the 7-day operational log TTL.
- Complete the attached exception form and return to us (per Camila's note) by EOD Friday.

Rafael Mendes
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
